slides.texte_overlay:
Habits of men who
are never bored
They turn errands into small adventures. A different route to work, a new café for coffee, a walk through a park they've never visited. Novelty hides in small changes.
They ask strangers interesting questions. The taxi driver, the old man at the bus stop, the shop owner. Everyone has a story, and curious men collect them.
They keep a notebook of ideas. Business ideas, trip plans, things to learn. When a free afternoon appears, they always have a list of exciting things to start.
They feed their curiosity daily. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and every walk or museum visit suddenly has a story behind it.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now every walk or museum visit suddenly has a story behind it.

slides.texte_overlay: They make things with their hands. Cooking a new recipe, building a shelf, fixing a bike. Creating something real is one of the best cures for boredom.
They plan something to look forward to. A trip next month, a concert, a weekend away. Having something on the calendar keeps the weeks full of energy.
They switch off the screen when they're bored. Instead of scrolling, they go outside, call a friend or pick up a book. Boredom is often just too much screen.
